result.title: Can LLM Agents Organize Their Own Memory?
result.summary: In most LLM agents, weights are fixed after deployment, so new information must be retained in external memory. Existing approaches often rely on predefined records and fixed organizational rules, which cannot readily accommodate evolving tasks and interactions. This raises the question: can LLM agents organize their own memory using ordinary documents? We introduce self-organized memory (SoMem), a framework that stores memory in linked documents. The agent decides what to summarize, how to group related information, and when to revise existing topics, and every summary it produces stays linked to the original interactions as evidence. The runtime validates updates and automatically derives temporal, relational, and recent-memory views from the organized content. At query time, the agent chooses what to search and read, following document links and inspecting original evidence as needed. On LoCoMo, BEAM-100K, and LongMemEval-S, SoMem outperforms the strongest baseline by 2.66, 3.10, and 2.00 percentage points, respectively. The constructed memory can be reused across models, and additional reasoning effort can further improve answer quality. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of agents organizing and using their own persistent memory through ordinary documents. Code is available at: https://github.com/Qi202/SoMem.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SoMem 框架，让 LLM agent 用互链文档自组织外部记忆：自主决定摘要什么、如何分组、何时修订已有主题，每条摘要保留原始交互作为证据，查询时自行选择检索与阅读路径，在 LoCoMo 等长时记忆基准上优于最强基线。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作不涉及视觉或多模态推理，但「摘要条目始终链回原始证据」「运行时校验更新」「查询时自主决定读什么、读到哪」可能为 LVR 中的视觉证据保真与 LOOK/STOP 决策表述提供概念线索，值得核查。
